title: Read the bytes of a dump from a ticket, and refuse what you can't be sure of

blocks.text: Last month a test built from a ticket passed, the ticket was closed, and the purchase failed again the next morning. The bytes in the test were not the bytes in the ticket, and nothing had said so.

From now on the team turns every dump into bytes with `HexDumpReader.read`, in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/HexDumpReader.java`. The dumps it gets come from the acquirer's support desk (made with `hexdump -C`), from our own channel's log events, and from colleagues who paste them into chat and mail. `read` already splits a dump into lines, skips blank ones and collects the bytes. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `parse`: one line of a dump, as the offset it states and the bytes it shows;
`check`: whether that line can come next.

blocks.text: When you're done, `read` returns exactly the bytes the dump shows, or throws `IllegalArgumentException` when it can't be sure of them. It never returns other bytes. About 25 lines in total.

The tests use an authorization from another terminal, dumped by jPOS and by `hexdump -C`, copied whole, with lines lost or pasted twice, with a byte position damaged, and with text columns that happen to look like hex.

cases.says: the output of ISOUtil.hexdump reads back to the same bytes, for full and short last lines
a dump of a packed authorization reads back to bytes that unpack completely to the same fields
blank lines and CRLF line endings are ignored, and an empty dump is no bytes
a text column whose characters look like hex pairs is not read as bytes
a line whose offset is not the number of bytes read before it, because a line was lost or pasted twice, is refused
the hexdump -C layout, with eight-digit offsets, a barred text column and a final offset-only line, reads to the same bytes
hex digits in lower case, as hexdump -C writes them, are read
spaces in front of the offset, as in a log event's first dump line, are not part of the columns
a byte position holding something other than two hex digits, or a line without an offset, is refused

origin.section: 17.1 A Dump Is Evidence Only When It Reads Back to the Bytes It Shows

concepts: A dump from outside is evidence only when it reads back to the bytes it shows: decodeHexDump reads one layout and checks nothing, so a reader checks each line's offset and reads bytes from their columns.
